title: Nasdaq, Dow, S&P 500 Forecast: Rising Yields Test Bulls
detail:
Nasdaq, Dow, S&P 500 Forecast: Rising Yields Test Bulls
Christopher Lewis
Tue, September 8, 2026 at 8:37 AM CDT 3 min read
^NDX
^GSPC
NASDAQ 100 Technical Analysis
Daily price chart for NAS100 showing price at 29,583.8, holding above the 50 EMA (29,241.8) and 200 EMA (27,432.8). Source: TradingView

The Nasdaq 100 looks as if it is relatively resilient considering everything that's going on around the world right now, with the Nasdaq 100 trying to rally early in the day.

It'll be interesting to see if there's any type of follow-through as New York comes on. Keep in mind that oil and the inflation risk continue to be a major problem, and the Federal Reserve repricing is out there as well, with the Friday payroll gain of 162,000 versus the roughly 55,000 expected. It has pushed rate hike probabilities toward 60%.

Semiconductors continue to perform well in this index. It looks more or less like sustained upward pressure, but not enough to get overly aggressive.

Dow Jones 30 Technical Analysis
Daily price chart for US30 showing price at 53,034.1 bouncing along the lower boundary of an ascending channel and above the 50 EMA (52,818.8). Source: TradingView

The Dow Jones 30 has shown itself to be somewhat resilient, with the 50-day EMA sitting just below. It's the laggard of the three, though, not by much.

Right now there are some stocks worth watching. Amgen is down 5% pre-market. Novartis reported disappointing clinical trials, and because Amgen has exposure to a competing cardiovascular treatment, it seems like that's coming into the picture as well.

This is estimated to be about 120 points of Dow decline, potentially.

The fundamental backdrop, again, is oil inflation expectations. The 10-year Treasury is hovering right around 4.78%. Energy exposure is benefiting in the Dow, so keep that in mind.

S&P 500 Technical Analysis
Daily price chart for SP500 showing price at 7,710.52, consolidating above the 50 EMA (7,616.19) and 200 EMA (7,211.86). Source: TradingView

The S&P 500 looks like it's trying to turn things around after initially dropping a little bit. Right now, the Brent story and Light Sweet Crude, of course, are both influencing this market.

The most important number might be 4.8% because it seems like when we get above there, it causes a little bit of a negative reaction.

7,800 above is significant resistance. The fulcrum price, if you will, the pivot price, seems to be 7,700, so it's worth watching.

We do have PPI on Thursday and CPI on Friday, and, of course, the Federal Reserve rate decision next week. So, a little bit of choppiness, but it does look like if we can get yields to drop a little bit, the S&P 500 gets a little happier.

title: SpaceX Set for Boost From Potential Jump in Nasdaq 100 Weighting
detail:
SpaceX Set for Boost From Potential Jump in Nasdaq 100 Weighting
SpaceX Set for Boost From Potential Jump in Nasdaq 100 Weighting · Bloomberg · Bloomberg
Carmen Reinicke and Yiqin Shen
Tue, September 8, 2026 at 6:00 AM CDT 5 min read
SPCX
NDAQ
^NDX
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

(Bloomberg) -- SpaceX's stock has been stuck in a tight trading range recently, but a wave of new buying may soon arrive when the Nasdaq 100 Index goes through its quarterly rebalancing later this month.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Trump Says Canada's Dollar 'Imbalance' With US Is Unacceptable

Indonesia's Richest Family Moves More Than $1 Billion Offshore

Canada Imposes Tariffs Up to 50% on US, Risking Wider Trade War

Sapporo Beer Moving Production to US From Canada on Tariffs

Iran Says Strait of Hormuz Deal With Oman Just Days Away

The key is the combination of a little-discussed rule in the tech-heavy benchmark's construction and a staggered series of lockup periods for shareholders of Elon Musk's satellite and space exploration venture that has limited the number of shares available to trade.

Nasdaq Inc. determines a company's weighting in the index based on a calculation of its market value that factors in either its total outstanding shares or three times its free-floating shares, whichever is lower. This means a stock with a low free float, which excludes shares held by insiders or those subject to lockups, will not have its full market value used to calculate its weighting.

For SpaceX, which has a relatively small free float because of lockup restrictions, that leaves it with a weighting of 1.25% in the Nasdaq 100, which is 19th biggest, despite sporting the sixth largest market capitalization in the index at more than $2 trillion.

But that weighting is expected to rise after the index's next rebalancing, which is set to be announced on Friday after the bell and take effect on Sept. 21. That's due in part to the fact that more than one billion shares have now been released from lock-up restrictions, boosting its free float to nearly 30% of SpaceX's outstanding shares from less than 10% immediately after the IPO.

SpaceX's weighting could hit 2.25% after the rebalance, forcing $15.5 billion of net passive buying from index funds and ETFs, according to estimates by JPMorgan Securities strategists led by Min Moon. Roughly $1.7 trillion in assets track the Nasdaq 100 as of the end of second quarter, according to Nasdaq, including the Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1 exchange-traded fund, better known by its ticker symbol QQQ.

As more SpaceX shares are unlocked over the next year, the company's free float will continue to rise, meaning its Nasdaq 100 weighting could potentially increase even more.

"The market price is going to get shoved around here by, to some degree, forced buying," said Ed O'Gorman, chief executive officer at River Wealth Advisors. "It is going be some time until I think you really get a good read on what the market truly thinks about the stock."

title: Dow Futures Fall as Markets Assess Fed Rate Expectations and Higher Oil Prices
detail:
Dow Futures Fall as Markets Assess Fed Rate Expectations and Higher Oil Prices
Fiona Craig
Tue, September 8, 2026 at 3:45 AM CDT 2 min read
CL=F
^NDX
^DJI
^GSPC

U.S. stock futures were mixed early Tuesday as investors returned from the Labor Day holiday and assessed higher oil prices, recent employment data and expectations for the Federal Reserve's September policy meeting.

Dow Jones Futures fell 0.8% to 53,034.0 points by 03:13 ET (07:13 GMT), while S&P 500 Futures declined 0.2% to 7,704.75 points. Nasdaq 100 Futures moved in the opposite direction, rising 0.2% to 29,609.75 points.

U.S. markets were closed on Monday for Labor Day, leaving investors to respond to Friday's employment report alongside developments in the Middle East.

Markets Increase Expectations for September Fed Rate Hike

U.S. employers added 162,000 jobs in August, exceeding economists' expectations, while the unemployment rate remained at 4.1%.

Following the report, futures markets were pricing an approximately 60% probability of a 25-basis-point interest-rate increase at the Federal Reserve's Sept. 15-16 meeting, according to CME FedWatch. That compared with a probability of 49% before the employment data.

UBS revised its monetary policy forecast on Monday and now expects two Federal Reserve rate increases during 2026, one in September and another in December. The bank had previously expected rates to remain unchanged this year.

These forecasts and market-implied probabilities represent expectations rather than established future policy decisions.

U.S. Inflation Data in Focus

Investors are awaiting further inflation data later this week, with producer prices scheduled for Thursday and consumer prices due on Friday.

The figures will provide additional information on inflation ahead of the Federal Reserve's September meeting and could influence market expectations for the central bank's next policy decision.

Higher energy prices have also returned to focus as investors assess the inflation outlook.

Brent crude traded around $97 a barrel on Tuesday amid escalating tensions between the United States and Iran and concerns about potential disruption to energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran has threatened retaliation against regional energy infrastructure following U.S. strikes on Iranian vessels, while reports of attacks on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery added to concerns about energy supplies.

Sustained increases in energy prices could add to inflationary pressures, although their eventual effect on Federal Reserve policy will depend on economic data and policymakers' assessment.

Wall Street Closed Lower on Friday

Major U.S. equity indices ended Friday's session lower following the August employment report.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.5%, while the S&P 500 fell 0.4% and the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.3%.

Markets are now assessing the combination of upcoming inflation data, developments in energy markets and expectations for the Federal Reserve's Sept. 15-16 meeting.

Apple (AAPL) stock has seen a reversal of fortunes of sorts. It underperformed the Nasdaq 100 Index ($IUXX) in the first half of the year but has since raced ahead and is now outperforming the tech-heavy index. Apple's price action over the previous couple of years was dampened by lingering concerns that it was lagging in the artificial intelligence (AI) race as investors chased names seen as AI winners.

www.barchart.com
Magnificent 7 Stocks Have Looked Weak

However, the situation has flipped over the last couple of months. Investors are now getting increasingly wary of tech companies' ever-rising capex to build AI infrastructure. For context, among its Magnificent 7 peers, Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), and Tesla (TSLA) raised their respective 2026 capex budgets, while Meta Platforms (META) raised the lower end of the guidance by $5 billion. However, it maintained the upper end at $145 billion.

Microsoft (MSFT) stood out as the company not only maintained its capex guidance for the current calendar year but said that it expects to generate positive free cash flows next year despite an expected increase in capex, which I believe are the golden words markets want to hear from hyperscalers. No wonder, MSFT rallied the most among Mag 7 peers following its June quarter earnings and has built on those gains, rising over $500 in the process.

Apple Flags Memory Shortage Issues

Apple stock plunged following its earnings, but that had nothing to do with its capex — far from it, actually, as the market's concern has been that the company is actually underspending on AI. The post-earnings decline was due to the guidance miss, as Apple blamed supply-side issues, particularly the memory shortage, taking a toll on sales as well as margins.

During the earnings call, Tim Cook — who stepped down as CEO Sept. 1 — said, "If you look beyond September, we see the market pricing for memory continuing to increase, which could drive an increasing impact on our business, and we're continuing to evaluate this."

Meanwhile, Apple has since recovered from the post-earnings crash and is up nearly 21% for the year, which for context is the highest among Mag 7 stocks, barring Nvidia (NVDA), which is up around 22.5%.

title: Polymarket Launches Crypto Perpetual Futures With Up to 20x Leverage
detail:
Polymarket Launches Crypto Perpetual Futures With Up to 20x Leverage
Jose Antonio Lanz

ETH-USD
SOL-USD
CL=F
Explore cryptocurrencies on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Polymarket, the prediction market platform that rose to fame during the 2024 presidential election, opened its perpetual futures product to traders on September 3, extending a platform built around yes-or-no election and sports bets into leveraged derivatives.

The new offering, called Perps, launched with an initial 10 markets—Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, HYPE, gold, silver, WTI oil, the S&P 500, the Nasdaq 100 and a contract tracking SpaceX shares—before expanding to 67 within hours, according to Polymarket's product page. Polymarket first teased the feature in April with a 10x leverage cap.

Myriad: When will Polymarket launch its token? Click to make your prediction.

Perpetual futures work nothing like Polymarket's usual contracts, which settle at $1 or zero once an event resolves. A perp instead tracks its underlying asset's price continuously with no expiration date, and a funding rate moves payments between long and short traders every hour to keep the contract anchored to spot. That funding rate is capped at 4% per hour in either direction.

Polymarket's documentation caps crypto, the S&P 500, oil, gold, and silver at 20x, while individual stocks and other real-world assets—Tesla, Nvidia, Apple and Coinbase among 36 listed equities—max out at 10x. Maintenance margin sits at half the maximum leverage rate, so a fully leveraged 20x position can be liquidated after losing roughly 2.5% of its posted margin.

Polymarket promoted the launch on X, pitching a compound trade: go long Bitcoin, bet on the Fed's next move, and short the S&P 500's reaction, all from one account. The company also billed the product as carrying the deepest liquidity and lowest fees among crypto perps venues.

None of it reaches Polymarket's American users. The company's own FAQ bars order placement from the United States, Canada, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Crimea, Donetsk, and Luhansk.

U.S. traders get routed to Polymarket US, a separate CFTC-regulated exchange. That split followed Polymarket's 2022 settlement with the CFTC, which fined the company $1.4 million and ordered it to wind down noncompliant contracts after finding it had run an unregistered swaps facility. It has since returned to the U.S., but in a more limited fashion.

Kalshi beat Polymarket to the U.S. market by more than three months. The CFTC approved Kalshi's Bitcoin perpetual futures contract on May 29, letting the rival prediction market call it the first onshore perpetual futures product in the country. Kalshi has since filed for perpetuals on a dozen altcoins and a separate copper contract.

The bigger competitive test is Hyperliquid, the decentralized exchange that already dominates on-chain perpetuals trading—and, which according to President Donald Trump himself, is working with the CFTC to open itself up to U.S. traders very soon.

A Bloomberg report recently furthered that talk, with news that Hyperliquid is already in negotiations with Kraken parent company Payward to do exactly that.

title: Wall Street Rallies as Fed’s Waller Hints at September Rate Hold: Stock Market Today
detail:
Wall Street Rallies as Fed’s Waller Hints at September Rate Hold: Stock Market Today
Piero Cingari
Thu, September 3, 2026 at 12:47 PM CDT 7 min read
^NDX

U.S. stocks rallied broadly at midday Thursday, bouncing off the four-session slide that had dragged the Nasdaq 100 back below its August close, after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller signaled he could back leaving interest rates on hold this month.

"If there is continued progress toward our 2% goal, then I am willing to support holding the policy rate at its current level," Waller said.

Traders now price in roughly a 50% probability of a September rate hike, down from about 70% earlier in the week.

That was enough to spark a broad-based relief rally, with the most rate-sensitive corners of the market – software, small caps and anything crypto-linked – leading the bounce.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury note eased to 4.75%, down 4 basis points, after touching 4.81% earlier in the week, its highest level since October 2023. The rate-sensitive 2-year yield fell 5 basis points to 4.34%, while the 30-year held at 5.23%, down 3 basis points.

The dollar index slid to 99, a near two-week low, with the greenback dropping 2.1% against the yen after a potential new intervention from Tokyo.

That dollar weakness lit a fire under Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC), which surged 4.6% to about $80,900, dragging the entire listed crypto complex higher.

The S&P 500 rose 0.96% to 7,740.14, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average outperformed with a 1.1% advance, adding 597 points to 53,658.71.

The Nasdaq 100 climbed 1.0% to 29,439.78. Within Magnificent Seven stocks, Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA) jumped 7.4%, Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) added 3.8% and Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT) rose 3.3%, while Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL) gained 1.7%.

Data flow was constructive. The ISM Services PMI jumped to 55.4 in August from 54.1, beating the 54.3 consensus and marking the strongest services expansion in six months, though the prices-paid subindex spiked to a four-year high of 72.6.

Gold pushed toward the $4,500 handle, rising 2.4% to $4,492 an ounce as the dollar and real yields retreated.
